financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone) basis. total_liabilities = non-current (165,307,193) + current (2,832,119,855) = 2,997,427,048 (filing does not print a Company-level total-liabilities subtotal directly, derived by summation). short_term_borrowings = current Interest bearing loans and borrowings (1,431,478,189) + Bank Overdrafts (12,296,411) = 1,443,774,600. capex = PPE (29,885,030) + intangibles (1,586,586) = 31,471,616. finance_costs here is materially less cushioned by FX gain than the Group figure (Company finance cost -12% YoY vs Group -71%), which is why Company PBT fell 35% YoY even as Group PBT was flat -- see GROUP row notes.

JAT Holdings PLC (wood coatings/paints manufacturer, plus brushes/rollers, decoratives, furnishing, EV chargers). operating_profit = 'Results from Operating Activities' (173,757,804), the filing's own subtotal before finance cost/income and JV results. finance_costs = 'Finance cost' per Note 5 (26,994,212), which nets Interest on Loans and Borrowings (78,323,167) + Interest on Lease Liabilities (5,382,574) + Foreign Exchange (Gain)/Loss (-56,711,529 gain) -- the large FX gain this quarter is the primary reason reported finance cost fell 71% YoY, NOT lower interest expense (interest on loans and borrowings was roughly flat, +3% YoY); this is called out explicitly in the narrative below since it's material to interpreting the flat PBT. short_term_borrowings = current 'Interest bearing loans and borrowings' (2,677,330,658) + 'Bank Overdrafts' (276,814,799) = 2,954,145,457; long_term_borrowings = non-current 'Interest bearing loans and borrowings' (362,798,155). capex = 'Purchase and constructions of property, plant & equipment' (43,159,264) + 'Acquisition of intangible assets' (1,586,586) = 44,745,850. EPS cross-check: 152,705,380 (equity holders' profit) / 522,436,476 shares = 0.2923 ~= disclosed 0.29 -- ties. No column-swap issues found.

interim_updates.note_text: JAT Holdings' Group revenue grew 34% YoY to Rs.3.04bn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), driven mainly by the Wood coatings product line (+41% YoY to Rs.2.40bn, ~79% of Group revenue) and by overseas growth -- Bangladesh revenue +43% and a new New Zealand contribution of Rs.338.6mn (Mirotone NZ Limited, not present in the prior-year comparative). Gross profit grew a slower 29% (Rs.830.2mn to Rs.1,072.1mn) as cost of sales grew 37%, and Results from Operating Activities actually fell 25% to Rs.173.8mn (from Rs.230.6mn) as Selling & Distribution expenses (+36%) and Administrative expenses (+40%) both outgrew gross profit, and Other Income fell 75% (Rs.61.7mn to Rs.15.3mn, mainly the absence of a prior-year Rs.10mn PPE disposal gain and a Rs.10mn biological-asset fair-value gain). Despite the 25% operating-profit decline, Group PBT was flat YoY (Rs.167.0mn vs Rs.166.4mn) because Finance Cost fell 71% (Rs.93.3mn to Rs.27.0mn) -- but this is entirely a foreign-exchange effect, not an interest-cost improvement: per the filing's own Note 5, Interest on Loans and Borrowings was roughly flat (+3% YoY, Rs.75.9mn to Rs.78.3mn) while Foreign Exchange swung from a Rs.14.0mn loss to a Rs.56.7mn gain. The standalone Company (mostly Sri Lanka operations) shows the underlying deterioration more clearly, since its FX-driven finance-cost cushion was much smaller (Company finance cost -12% YoY vs Group's -71%): Company revenue grew only 7% (vs Group's 34%, confirming most growth came from overseas subsidiaries), Results from Operating Activities fell 35% (Rs.179.0mn to Rs.116.8mn), and PBT fell 35% (Rs.175.8mn to Rs.115.0mn). By product, EV Chargers revenue at Company level collapsed 98% (Rs.187.9mn to Rs.3.0mn), a large negative swing versus the prior-year quarter which had an unusually large EV Charger contribution.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for JAT -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Segmental detail above (Wood coatings, EV Chargers, geographic revenue) is by product/geography, not by profit-and-loss segment -- the filing does not disclose segment-level PBT or EBITDA, only segment revenue, so driver attribution is limited to the P&L/geographic/product-revenue detail actually disclosed.
interim_updates.takeaway: The Group's flat PBT headline conceals two real, offsetting effects: core operating profitability genuinely deteriorated (-25% YoY, cost growth in SD/Admin outpacing gross profit), and this was masked almost entirely by a large, non-operating foreign-exchange gain on the finance-cost line (not by lower interest expense, which was roughly flat). The standalone Company figures -- unflattered by that FX swing and without the new New Zealand/Bangladesh growth -- show the underlying picture more starkly: PBT -35% YoY, compounded by a near-total collapse in the EV Chargers product line.
operational_highlights: Group revenue +34% YoY to Rs.3.04bn, driven by Wood coatings (+41%, ~79% of revenue), Bangladesh (+43%), and a new New Zealand contribution (Mirotone NZ Limited, Rs.338.6mn, not in the prior-year comparative)
Group Results from Operating Activities -25% YoY to Rs.173.8mn as Selling & Distribution (+36%) and Administrative expenses (+40%) outgrew the 29% gross-profit growth

Group PBT flat YoY (Rs.167.0mn vs Rs.166.4mn) only because Finance Cost fell 71% -- driven by a swing from a Rs.14.0mn FX loss to a Rs.56.7mn FX gain (Note 5), while Interest on Loans and Borrowings itself was roughly flat (+3% YoY)
Standalone Company (mostly Sri Lanka): revenue +7% YoY (vs Group's +34%, confirming overseas subsidiaries drove most growth); Results from Operating Activities -35%; PBT -35% to Rs.115.0mn
EV Chargers product line collapsed at Company level: revenue -98% YoY (Rs.187.9mn to Rs.3.0mn) as the prior-year quarter had an unusually large contribution from this category
Other Income fell 75% YoY (Rs.61.7mn to Rs.15.3mn), mainly the absence of a prior-year PPE disposal gain (Rs.10.0mn) and biological-asset fair-value gain (Rs.10.0mn)
key_drivers: Wood coatings (the core product line, ~79% of Group revenue) grew 41% YoY and is the single largest driver of Group revenue growth

Group finance-cost improvement (-71% YoY) is a foreign-exchange effect, not an operating one -- Note 5 shows Interest on Loans and Borrowings roughly flat (+3%) while FX swung from a Rs.14.0mn loss to a Rs.56.7mn gain, fully explaining why Group PBT held flat despite a 25% operating-profit decline

New Zealand (Mirotone NZ Limited) contributed Rs.338.6mn of Group revenue this quarter with zero prior-year comparative -- an acquisition/new-entity effect inflating the YoY Group growth rate relative to organic performance
EV Chargers product line -98% YoY at Company level (Rs.187.9mn to Rs.3.0mn) is the largest single product-line swing and a material drag on Company-level results specifically

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
